attributes.references: ISO 8583, Visa Core Rules, Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: card_scheme
attributes.description: Payment network brand or card scheme involved in the interchange dispute.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules, Mastercard Rules, EMVCo

attributes.name: claimed_interchange_amount
attributes.description: Interchange fee amount claimed by the disputing party as the correct amount that should have been applied.

attributes.name: claimed_irf_category_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Claimed Interchange Reimbursement Fee (IRF) Category Code
attributes.description: The interchange rate category code that the disputing party claims should have been applied to the transaction or billing period.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the interchange dispute record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: cross_border_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the disputed transaction involved cross-border processing, which affects interchange qualification.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in the interchange dispute.

attributes.name: dispute_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the interchange dispute in the resolution workflow.

attributes.name: dispute_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interchange dispute based on the nature of the disagreement.

attributes.name: disputed_amount
attributes.description: The difference between the claimed and scheme-reported interchange amounts, representing the financial value in dispute.

attributes.name: durbin_regulated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the disputed transaction or billing period is subject to Durbin Amendment interchange fee caps for regulated debit cards.
attributes.references: Regulation II Durbin Amendment, Federal Reserve System

attributes.name: escalation_level
attributes.description: Current escalation level of the interchange dispute within the card scheme dispute resolution hierarchy.

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: Date when the interchange dispute was formally filed with the card scheme or counterparty.

attributes.name: filing_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the interchange dispute was submitted into the dispute management system.

attributes.name: financial_adjustment_amount
attributes.description: The final financial adjustment amount resulting from the dispute resolution, which may be positive (credit) or negative (debit).

attributes.name: initiator
attributes.description: Identifies which party initiated the interchange dispute (acquirer, issuer, payment platform, or card scheme).

attributes.name: mcc
attributes.description: Four-digit merchant category code associated with the disputed transaction, relevant for interchange qualification rules.
attributes.references: ISO 18245, Visa Core Rules, Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or internal observations related to the interchange dispute.

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the specific reason for the interchange dispute, aligned with card scheme dispute reason taxonomies.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules, Mastercard Rules, ISO 8583

attributes.name: reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual explanation of the reason for the interchange dispute, providing context beyond the reason code.

attributes.name: reference_number
attributes.description: External business identifier for the interchange dispute, used for communication with card schemes, acquirers, and issuers.

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: Date when the interchange dispute was resolved or closed, marking the end of the dispute lifecycle.

attributes.name: resolution_outcome
attributes.description: Final outcome of the interchange dispute resolution process, indicating whether the dispute was upheld, denied, or partially resolved.

attributes.name: resolution_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the interchange dispute resolution was recorded in the system.

attributes.name: respondent
attributes.description: Identifies which party is responding to or defending against the interchange dispute.

attributes.name: response_due_date
attributes.description: Deadline by which the respondent must provide a response to the interchange dispute, per card scheme rules.

attributes.name: scheme_applied_irf_category_code

attributes.description: The interchange rate category code that was actually applied by the card scheme, which is being disputed.

attributes.name: scheme_case_number
attributes.description: Case or dispute tracking number assigned by the card scheme for this interchange dispute.

attributes.name: scheme_reported_interchange_amount
attributes.description: Interchange fee amount reported or calculated by the card scheme, which is being disputed.

attributes.name: supporting_documentation_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or location of supporting documentation, evidence, or attachments related to the interchange dispute.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the interchange dispute record was last modified in the system.

The business actively manages this mapping, capturing effective dates and optional fee‑type overrides for each program‑schedule pair.

domains.name: fraud
domains.description: Operational domain for real-time fraud detection, case management, and prevention. Owns fraud scoring rule configurations, velocity controls, device fingerprint records, 3DS authentication outcomes, SCA challenge results, blocklists, and fraud case lifecycle tracking from detection through remediation.

products.name: fraud_case
products.description: Core operational record representing a fraud investigation lifecycle from initial detection through remediation. Tracks case type (card-not-present, account takeover, synthetic identity, first-party fraud, etc.), case status, assigned investigator, detection source, financial exposure, recovery amount, and resolution outcome. SSOT for fraud case management in the Fraud Detection and Prevention Platform.
products.reference: Fraud Case Management — FDPP Case Lifecycle

attributes.name: fraud_case_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the fraud case record.

attributes.name: assigned_investigator_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the analyst or investigator assigned to the case.

attributes.name: billing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to interchange.interchange_billing. Business justification: Billing adjustments for chargebacks require linking each fraud case to the billing period record that captured the transaction.

attributes.name: cardholder_profile_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the cardholder linked to the suspicious activity.

Distinct from exposure_limit (which governs merchant/cardholder limits) — this governs institutional counterparty risk.

products.name: rule_assignment
products.description: This association captures the operational assignment of risk decisioning rules to payment products. Each record links one risk_rule to one payment_product and stores the effective period and current status of that assignment.. Existence Justification: Risk rules are actively assigned to payment products by risk operations. A single risk_rule can be applied to many payment_product records, and each payment_product can have multiple risk_rule assignments, each with its own effective dates and status.

products.name: model_currency_pair_assignment
products.description: This association product captures the assignment of a risk scoring model to a specific currency pair, including the period during which the model is effective and the version of the model applied. Each record links one risk_model to one currency_pair and stores relationship‑specific attributes.. Existence Justification: Risk models are actively assigned to multiple currency pairs, and each currency pair can be evaluated by several risk models over time. The assignment is managed as a distinct operational record that includes effective dates and model version information. This many‑to‑many relationship is therefore a business concept that is created, updated, and retired by risk‑management teams.

domains.name: dispute
domains.description: Manages the full dispute and chargeback lifecycle — retrieval requests, chargeback filings, reason code classification, representment packages, arbitration tracking, evidence collection, response deadlines, and final resolution outcomes. SSOT for ARN-linked dispute records and financial adjustments per card scheme rules.
domains.references: Visa Core Rules, Mastercard Rules, Regulation E

products.name: chargeback
products.description: Core master record for a chargeback filing initiated by an issuing bank on behalf of a cardholder. Captures the full chargeback lifecycle from initial filing through final resolution, including ARN, originating transaction reference, card scheme reason code (FK to reference domain), financial adjustment amounts, cycle stage (first chargeback, second chargeback/pre-arbitration chargeback), filing timestamps, scheme-mandated response deadlines, actual response dates, deadline compliance status, and current disposition. SSOT for all chargeback records in the dispute domain per card scheme rules (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover).

attributes.name: chargeback_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate primary key for the chargeback record in the dispute domain. Serves as the SSOT identifier for all chargeback lifecycle tracking per card scheme rules (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: authorization_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transaction.authorization. Business justification: Original authorization data is required to validate the auth amount, response codes, and 3‑DS results during chargeback assessment.

attributes.name: capture_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transaction.capture. Business justification: Capture details (final amount, fees) are essential for reconciling chargeback amounts and settlement adjustments.

attributes.name: chargeback_reason_code_id
attributes.description: Reference to the card scheme reason code record in the reference domain that classifies the basis for the chargeback (e.g., fraud, not as described, duplicate processing, credit not processed). Each card scheme (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover) maintains its own reason code taxonomy.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules

attributes.name: cross_border_payment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fx.cross_border_payment. Business justification: Cross‑border chargebacks must reference the originating payment to satisfy audit, compliance, and settlement reconciliation.

attributes.name: dispute_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent dispute case record that initiated this chargeback filing. A dispute may progress through retrieval request, first chargeback, second chargeback, and arbitration stages — this links the chargeback to its overarching dispute case.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: dispute_dispute_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent dispute case record that initiated this chargeback filing. A dispute may progress through retrieval request, first chargeback, second chargeback, and arbitration stages — this links the chargeback to its overarching dispute case.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: ecosystem_partner_id
attributes.description: Reference to the issuing bank (cardholder's bank) that initiated the chargeback on behalf of the cardholder. The issuing bank is the party that files the chargeback against the acquiring bank per card scheme rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: journal_entry_id
attributes.description: Reference to the General Ledger entry in Oracle Financials (ERP) recording the financial adjustment associated with this chargeback. Enables reconciliation between the dispute management system and the financial accounting system for SOX compliance and revenue recognition.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); ERP - Oracle Financials; GAAP

attributes.name: merchant_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchant record against whom the chargeback has been filed. The Merchant Identification Number (MID) is the acquiring bank-assigned identifier for the merchant in the payment network.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Merchant Management System

attributes.name: payment_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.payment_product. Business justification: Chargeback performance dashboard requires product‑level metrics for risk analysis and scheme reporting; linking each chargeback to its payment_product enables this.

attributes.name: payment_txn_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transaction.payment_txn. Business justification: Chargeback investigations need the detailed payment transaction record for settlement, network, and device info – a standard compliance and reporting requirement.

attributes.name: pos_terminal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to terminal.pos_terminal. Business justification: Chargeback Terminal Performance Report requires linking each chargeback to its originating POS terminal to monitor terminal risk and compliance.

attributes.name: rate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fx.fx_rate. Business justification: Chargeback settlement report requires original FX rate for currency conversion of the chargeback amount.

attributes.name: response_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gateway.gateway_response. Business justification: Chargeback reconciliation needs the original acquirer response to verify decline reason, authorization code, and fraud flags.

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Chargebacks are filed under a specific card scheme; scheme_id enables scheme‑level chargeback reporting required by Visa/Mastercard compliance.

attributes.name: settlement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to settlement.settlement. Business justification: Chargeback settlement reports must link to the settlement record that includes the chargeback amount for traceability.

attributes.name: transaction_id
attributes.description: Reference to the originating payment transaction record in the transaction domain that is the subject of this chargeback filing. Links the chargeback to the full transaction detail including authorization, capture, and settlement data.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: wallet_transaction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to wallet.wallet_transaction. Business justification: Chargeback processing for wallet transactions requires linking each chargeback to the specific wallet transaction that was disputed, enabling accurate reconciliation and reporting.

attributes.name: acquirer_reference
attributes.description: Acquiring bank's internal reference number for this chargeback case. Used by the acquiring bank's operations team to track the chargeback in their internal systems and correlate with the card scheme case identifier.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: adjustment_amount
attributes.description: Net financial adjustment amount posted to the merchant's account as a result of this chargeback. Includes the chargeback amount plus any applicable scheme fees, processing fees, or interchange adjustments. Negative value indicates a debit to the merchant; positive value indicates a credit (e.g., upon successful representment).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: amount
attributes.description: Gross amount of the chargeback as filed by the issuing bank in the transaction currency. Represents the disputed amount that will be debited from the merchant's account if the chargeback is upheld. May differ from the original transaction amount in cases of partial chargebacks.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 4217; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: arbitration_deadline
attributes.description: Scheme-mandated deadline for filing an arbitration case with the card scheme after a failed pre-arbitration or second chargeback cycle. Arbitration is the final escalation path where the card scheme adjudicates the dispute and assigns liability. Missing this deadline forfeits the right to arbitration.

attributes.name: arbitration_filing_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual timestamp when the arbitration case was filed with the card scheme. Populated only when the chargeback has been escalated to the arbitration stage (cycle_stage = ARBITRATION).

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: Acquirer Reference Number uniquely identifying the originating payment transaction across the card scheme network. Primary linkage key between the chargeback and the settled transaction. Assigned by the acquiring bank at settlement and used by all parties to trace the transaction through the payment chain.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: card_scheme
attributes.description: Payment network brand (card scheme) under whose rules this chargeback is governed. Determines the applicable reason code taxonomy, response deadlines, cycle stages, and arbitration procedures. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: VISA|MASTERCARD|AMEX|DISCOVER|UNIONPAY|OTHER — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules; EMVCo

attributes.name: cardholder_dispute_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the cardholder's stated reason for disputing the transaction as captured by the issuing bank. Provides the narrative context behind the formal reason code classification. Used by the merchant in preparing the representment package.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: case_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the chargeback case as assigned by the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. Used by operations teams, merchants, and card schemes to reference the chargeback in correspondence, representment packages, and scheme portal submissions.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: chargeback_status
attributes.description: Current disposition and lifecycle status of the chargeback record. Tracks the chargeback from initial receipt through final resolution. RECEIVED: chargeback filed by issuer; UNDER_REVIEW: internal review in progress; AWAITING_RESPONSE: merchant response pending; REPRESENTED: merchant submitted representment; ACCEPTED: merchant accepted liability; WON: merchant successfully defended; LOST: chargeback upheld; ARBITRATION: escalated to scheme arbitration; CLOSED: final resolution reached. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: RECEIVED|UNDER_REVIEW|AWAITING_RESPONSE|REPRESENTED|ACCEPTED|WON|LOST|ARBITRATION|CLOSED — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the chargeback record was first created in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System (Silver Layer). Represents the system ingestion time, distinct from the filing_timestamp which is the business event time when the issuer filed the chargeback with the card scheme.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); GDPR Article 5; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the currency in which the chargeback amount is denominated. May differ from the original transaction currency in cross-border disputes where Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) was applied.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: cycle_stage
attributes.description: Current stage in the chargeback lifecycle cycle as defined by card scheme rules. FIRST_CHARGEBACK is the initial filing by the issuer; SECOND_CHARGEBACK (also called pre-arbitration chargeback under Mastercard rules) occurs after a failed representment; PRE_ARBITRATION is the Visa pre-arbitration stage; ARBITRATION is the final scheme-level adjudication; COMPLIANCE is a scheme compliance filing.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines

attributes.name: deadline_met
attributes.description: Indicates whether the chargeback response was submitted on or before the scheme-mandated response deadline. True if response_timestamp is on or before response_deadline; False if the deadline was missed, resulting in automatic acceptance of the chargeback liability.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: evidence_package_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the evidence package (representment documentation) submitted by the merchant to contest the chargeback. Points to the document management system location containing delivery confirmations, signed receipts, authorization records, and other supporting evidence.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: filing_timestamp
attributes.description: The principal business event timestamp recording when the chargeback was formally filed by the issuing bank with the card scheme. This is the scheme-recognized filing date used to calculate all response deadlines and compliance windows per card scheme rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583; Regulation E (Federal Reserve)

attributes.name: fraud_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this chargeback is classified as fraud-related based on the reason code category (True) or non-fraud (False). Fraud chargebacks (e.g., Visa reason code 10.x, Mastercard reason code 4837/4863) are tracked separately for fraud reporting, chargeback ratio monitoring, and Fraud Detection and Prevention Platform feedback loops.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS; FinCEN BSA

attributes.name: is_partial_chargeback
attributes.description: Indicates whether this chargeback is for a partial amount of the original transaction (True) or for the full transaction amount (False). Partial chargebacks occur when only a portion of the goods or services are disputed.

attributes.name: liability_party
attributes.description: The party determined to bear financial liability for the chargeback upon final resolution. MERCHANT: merchant absorbs the loss; ISSUER: issuing bank absorbs the loss; ACQUIRER: acquiring bank absorbs the loss; SCHEME: card scheme absorbs the loss (rare, typically in compliance cases).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines

attributes.name: original_transaction_amount
attributes.description: The full amount of the original payment transaction that is the subject of this chargeback, in the original transaction currency. Used to identify partial chargebacks where chargeback_amount is less than the full transaction amount.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: original_transaction_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the currency in which the original payment transaction was denominated. Enables currency reconciliation in cross-border dispute scenarios involving Foreign Exchange (FX) or Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC).
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: ratio_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this chargeback has been flagged as contributing to the merchant's chargeback ratio threshold breach under card scheme monitoring programs (e.g., Visa Chargeback Monitoring Program - VCMP, Mastercard Excessive Chargeback Program - ECP). Merchants exceeding scheme thresholds face fines and potential termination.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS

attributes.name: representment_deadline
attributes.description: Scheme-mandated deadline by which the merchant must submit a representment (rebuttal) package to challenge the chargeback. Distinct from response_deadline in that it specifically governs the representment submission window after the merchant elects to contest the chargeback.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: representment_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual timestamp when the merchant submitted the representment package to contest the chargeback. A representment is the merchant's formal response disputing the chargeback, including evidence such as delivery confirmation, signed receipts, or fraud documentation.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: resolution_outcome
attributes.description: Final resolution outcome of the chargeback after all dispute cycles are exhausted. MERCHANT_WON: representment was successful and chargeback reversed; ISSUER_WON: chargeback upheld and merchant debited; SPLIT_LIABILITY: liability shared between parties; WITHDRAWN: cardholder or issuer withdrew the dispute; EXPIRED: chargeback expired due to inaction.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules

attributes.name: resolution_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the chargeback reached its final resolution and the case was closed. Marks the end of the chargeback lifecycle. Used for SLA compliance measurement and financial reconciliation timing.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: response_deadline
attributes.description: Scheme-mandated deadline by which the acquiring bank or merchant must submit a representment or accept the chargeback. Calculated from the filing timestamp per card scheme rules (e.g., Visa typically allows 30 calendar days; Mastercard 45 calendar days). Missing this deadline results in automatic chargeback acceptance.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules

attributes.name: response_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual timestamp when the merchant or acquiring bank submitted their response (representment package or acceptance) to the chargeback. Compared against response_deadline to determine deadline compliance status.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: scheme_case_reference
attributes.description: Card scheme-assigned case identifier for the chargeback as provided by Visa, Mastercard, Amex, or Discover through their dispute resolution portals (e.g., Visa Resolve Online - VROL, Mastercard MATCH). Used for scheme-level tracking and arbitration submissions.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules

attributes.name: scheme_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged by the card scheme (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover) for processing the chargeback. Scheme fees are assessed per chargeback filing and may vary by scheme, reason code, and merchant chargeback ratio tier. Debited from the acquiring bank and typically passed through to the merchant.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules

attributes.name: sla_breach
attributes.description: Indicates whether the internal SLA for chargeback processing was breached (True) for this case. Internal SLAs govern the time from chargeback receipt to merchant notification, evidence collection, and representment submission, distinct from the scheme-mandated response deadlines.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Internal SLA Policy

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system of record from which this chargeback record was sourced (e.g., Dispute and Chargeback Management System). Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation across the lakehouse architecture.
attributes.references: Data Warehouse and Analytics Platform; SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act)

attributes.name: transaction_date
attributes.description: The date on which the original payment transaction that is the subject of this chargeback was processed. Used to verify chargeback filing timeliness against scheme-mandated windows (e.g., Visa allows chargebacks up to 120 days from transaction date in most cases).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Regulation E (Federal Reserve)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the chargeback record in the system. Tracks the last modification across any field in the chargeback lifecycle, supporting audit trail requirements and change detection for downstream data consumers.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); GDPR Article 5; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

products.name: retrieval_request
products.description: Pre-chargeback inquiry record issued by an issuing bank requesting transaction documentation (sales draft, receipt, authorization record) from the acquiring bank before a formal chargeback is filed. Tracks retrieval request ID, ARN, MID, TID, request date, fulfillment deadline, fulfillment status, and document delivery method. Failure to fulfill a retrieval request within scheme deadlines typically escalates to a chargeback.

attributes.name: retrieval_request_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the retrieval request record in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. Primary key for this entity. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.

attributes.name: assigned_analyst_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the dispute operations analyst assigned to manage the fulfillment of this retrieval request. Used for workload management, SLA accountability, and case ownership tracking.

attributes.name: card_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.reference_card_scheme. Business justification: Retrieval requests follow scheme‑specific documentation requirements; reference needed for compliance.

attributes.name: chargeback_id
attributes.description: Reference to the chargeback record that was escalated from this retrieval request when fulfillment was not completed within the scheme deadline. Null if the retrieval request was fulfilled and no chargeback was filed.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the dispute operations analyst assigned to manage the fulfillment of this retrieval request. Used for workload management, SLA accountability, and case ownership tracking.

attributes.name: pos_terminal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to terminal.pos_terminal. Business justification: Regulatory retrieval requests must capture the POS terminal ID to locate the original device for audit and evidence collection.

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Retrieval requests must comply with scheme‑specific documentation standards; scheme_id provides the reference for compliance audits.

attributes.name: acquirer_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the acquiring bank responsible for fulfilling the retrieval request by providing the requested transaction documentation to the issuing bank.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: Acquirer Reference Number uniquely identifying the original payment transaction that is the subject of this retrieval request. The ARN is the primary linkage between the retrieval request and the underlying transaction across card scheme networks. Critical for dispute lifecycle traceability.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: authorization_code
attributes.description: Authorization approval code issued by the issuing bank for the original transaction. Included in the retrieval request to help locate the original transaction record and validate the authorization record as part of the evidence package.
attributes.references: ISO 8583; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Payment Gateway and Authorization Engine

attributes.name: billing_amount
attributes.description: Amount billed to the cardholder in their billing currency, which may differ from the transaction amount when Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) or foreign exchange conversion was applied. Used in cross-border dispute resolution.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PSD2

attributes.name: billing_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code of the cardholder's billing currency. Relevant when DCC was applied and the billing currency differs from the transaction currency.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: bin
attributes.description: Bank Identification Number (BIN), also known as Issuer Identification Number (IIN), representing the first 6-8 digits of the PAN. Identifies the issuing bank and card product type. Used for scheme routing and issuer identification in the retrieval request workflow.
attributes.references: ISO 7812; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: cardholder_dispute_category
attributes.description: High-level category of the cardholder's dispute underlying the retrieval request. Aligns with card scheme dispute category frameworks (Visa Dispute Resolution; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Management). Used for dispute analytics and trend reporting.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; CFPB; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this retrieval request record was first created in the system of record. Maps to RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; SOX

attributes.name: days_to_fulfill
attributes.description: Number of calendar days elapsed between the request_date and the fulfillment_date. Populated upon fulfillment. Used for SLA performance analytics and scheme compliance benchmarking.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: document_delivery_method
attributes.description: Method used to deliver the requested transaction documentation (sales draft, receipt, authorization record) to the issuing bank. Electronic delivery via scheme portal is the preferred method per PCI DSS and scheme rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: document_types_requested
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or description of the specific document types requested by the issuing bank (e.g., sales draft, transaction receipt, authorization record, imprinted voucher, signed cardholder receipt). Drives the fulfillment workflow and evidence package assembly.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: documents_provided
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether all requested transaction documentation has been provided to the issuing bank. True when the fulfillment package is complete and delivered; False when pending or partially fulfilled.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: escalated_to_chargeback
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this retrieval request was escalated to a formal chargeback due to non-fulfillment within the scheme-mandated deadline. True indicates a chargeback has been filed; False indicates the request was resolved without chargeback escalation.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: escalation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the retrieval request was escalated to a formal chargeback. Populated only when escalated_to_chargeback is True. Used for SLA tracking and scheme compliance reporting.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: fraud_suspected
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the retrieval request is associated with a suspected fraudulent transaction, as flagged by the issuing bank or the fraud detection platform. When True, the case may be escalated to the Fraud Detection and Prevention Platform for additional investigation.
attributes.references: Fraud Detection and Prevention Platform; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; FinCEN BSA

attributes.name: fulfillment_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the acquiring bank fulfilled the retrieval request by delivering the requested documentation to the issuing bank. Null if not yet fulfilled. Used to calculate response time and SLA compliance.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: fulfillment_deadline
attributes.description: Scheme-mandated deadline by which the acquiring bank must fulfill the retrieval request by delivering the requested documentation. Failure to meet this deadline typically results in automatic escalation to a chargeback. Calculated from request_date per applicable card scheme rules (Visa: typically 30 days; Mastercard: varies by reason code).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS

attributes.name: fulfillment_status
attributes.description: Current fulfillment status of the retrieval request indicating whether the acquiring bank has delivered the required documentation within the scheme deadline. Maps to LIFECYCLE_STATUS category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. 'escalated_to_chargeback' indicates the request was not fulfilled and a formal chargeback has been filed.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: issuer_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the issuing bank (cardholder's bank) that originated the retrieval request. The issuing bank initiates the pre-chargeback inquiry to obtain transaction documentation. Maps to PARTY_REFERENCE category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: mcc
attributes.description: ISO 18245 four-digit Merchant Category Code classifying the type of business conducted by the merchant at the time of the original transaction. Used in dispute analysis and scheme reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 18245; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: merchant_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the merchant's country of operation where the original transaction occurred. Used for cross-border dispute routing and applicable scheme rule determination.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: merchant_name
attributes.description: Doing-business-as name of the merchant as it appears on the cardholder's statement for the original transaction. Used to identify the merchant in the retrieval request workflow and for cardholder communication.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Merchant Management System

attributes.name: mid
attributes.description: Merchant Identification Number of the merchant whose transaction is subject to the retrieval request. Assigned by the acquiring bank during merchant onboarding. Used to route fulfillment obligations to the correct merchant.
attributes.references: Merchant Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: pan_last_four
attributes.business_glossary_term: Primary Account Number (PAN) Last Four Digits
attributes.description: Last four digits of the cardholder's Primary Account Number (PAN) associated with the original transaction. Stored in truncated form per PCI DSS requirements to enable transaction identification without exposing full card data.
attributes.references: PCI DSS Requirement 3; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: pos_entry_mode
attributes.description: Method by which the cardholder's payment credentials were captured at the point of sale for the original transaction (e.g., EMV chip, magnetic stripe swipe, NFC contactless, manual key entry, e-commerce). Relevant to determining liability and document requirements in the retrieval request.
attributes.references: EMVCo; ISO 8583; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Card scheme reason code classifying the basis for the retrieval request (e.g., cardholder does not recognize transaction, potential fraud, copy request). Reason codes are scheme-specific (Visa and Mastercard maintain separate code sets). Drives document requirements and fulfillment obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product as codes vary extensively by scheme]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: reason_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the reason for the retrieval request corresponding to the reason_code. Provides context for operations teams handling the fulfillment workflow.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this retrieval request is subject to regulatory reporting obligations (e.g., CFPB complaint reporting, FinCEN SAR-related inquiry, GDPR data subject request). Triggers inclusion in compliance reporting workflows.
attributes.references: CFPB; FinCEN; GDPR Article 30; SOX; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: request_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the retrieval request was formally issued by the issuing bank. This is the principal business event date that starts the fulfillment deadline clock per card scheme rules. Maps to BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: response_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by the acquiring bank or merchant operations team describing the fulfillment response, any issues encountered in locating documentation, or reasons for non-fulfillment. Supports case management and audit trail.

attributes.name: retrieval_request_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the retrieval request, typically assigned by the card scheme or issuing bank. Used for cross-system tracking and scheme correspondence (e.g., Visa or Mastercard retrieval reference number). Maps to BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: scheme_case_number
attributes.description: Case or reference number assigned by the card scheme (Visa or Mastercard) to track this retrieval request within their dispute management systems. Used for scheme correspondence and audit trail.

attributes.name: sla_breach
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the fulfillment deadline was breached (i.e., the retrieval request was not fulfilled within the card scheme's mandated response window). True indicates an SLA breach; used for operational performance monitoring and scheme compliance reporting.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the operational system of record from which this retrieval request record was ingested into the Silver Layer (e.g., Dispute and Chargeback Management System). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Data Warehouse and Analytics Platform

attributes.name: tid
attributes.description: Terminal Identification Number identifying the specific POS or mPOS terminal at which the original transaction was processed. Supports evidence collection and sales draft retrieval from the correct terminal.

attributes.name: transaction_amount
attributes.description: Gross monetary amount of the original payment transaction subject to this retrieval request, expressed in the transaction currency. Used to validate documentation and assess potential chargeback financial exposure.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583; PCI DSS

attributes.name: transaction_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code of the original transaction amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for accurate financial exposure assessment and cross-border dispute handling.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: transaction_date
attributes.description: Date on which the original payment transaction subject to this retrieval request was processed. Used to verify transaction age against scheme retrieval request eligibility windows and to locate the original sales draft.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this retrieval request record was last modified in the system of record. Maps to RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Tracks status changes, fulfillment updates, and escalation events. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; SOX

products.name: representment
products.description: Merchant or acquirer response package submitted to rebut a chargeback filing. Captures representment ID, linked chargeback ID, ARN, submission timestamp, representment amount, evidence package reference, rebuttal narrative, scheme-specific representment reason code (FK to reference domain), submission channel, scheme-mandated response deadline, actual submission date, deadline compliance status, and outcome decision (accepted, rejected, escalated to pre-arbitration). Tracks the full representment lifecycle including pre-arbitration escalation eligibility.
products.reference: Card Scheme Representment / Second Presentment Rules

attributes.name: representment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the representment record in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. Primary key for the representment data product. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — a discrete business event (merchant/acquirer rebuttal package) with its own lifecycle.

attributes.name: card_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.reference_card_scheme. Business justification: Scheme‑specific representment windows are enforced; reference ensures correct rule lookup.

attributes.name: chargeback_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent chargeback filing that this representment is rebutting. Links the representment to its originating dispute event in the chargeback lifecycle.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: dispute_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the overarching dispute case that encompasses the chargeback and representment. Provides traceability to the full dispute lifecycle record in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System.

attributes.name: dispute_dispute_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the overarching dispute case that encompasses the chargeback and representment. Provides traceability to the full dispute lifecycle record in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System.

attributes.name: ecosystem_partner_id
attributes.description: Reference to the acquiring bank (merchant's bank) responsible for submitting the representment on behalf of the merchant. The acquiring bank is the primary party in the representment process per card scheme rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: financial_adjustment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the financial adjustment record in the ERP (Oracle Financials) or settlement system generated upon acceptance of the representment. Links the dispute outcome to the corresponding GL/AR credit entry.
attributes.references: SOX; ERP - Oracle Financials; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: mcc_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.mcc. Business justification: Representments are evaluated by merchant category; linking to reference.mcc supports fee and risk analysis.

attributes.name: merchant_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchant entity submitting the representment. The Merchant Identification Number (MID) identifies the acquiring merchant in the dispute rebuttal process.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Merchant Management System

attributes.name: payment_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.payment_product. Business justification: Representment fee calculation and settlement cycles depend on the underlying payment_product; the FK enables accurate fee application.

attributes.name: pos_terminal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to terminal.pos_terminal. Business justification: Representment filings often include terminal logs; linking to the POS terminal enables tracking representment outcomes per terminal.

attributes.name: response_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gateway.gateway_response. Business justification: Representment outcome analysis depends on the post‑representment gateway response to assess acquirer decision and any additional fees.

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Representments are evaluated according to the originating card scheme's rules; scheme_id is required for the Representment Decision Engine.

attributes.name: amount
attributes.description: The monetary amount being contested in the representment, typically equal to or less than the original chargeback amount. Represents the gross base amount the merchant/acquirer is seeking to recover.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: Acquirer Reference Number (ARN) linking the representment to the original transaction. A 23-digit identifier assigned by the acquiring bank used to trace the transaction across card scheme networks and issuer systems.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: assigned_analyst
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the dispute analyst or team responsible for preparing and managing this representment case. Supports workload management and accountability tracking within the Dispute and Chargeback Management System.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; SOX

attributes.name: chargeback_amount
attributes.description: The original chargeback amount as filed by the issuing bank. Retained on the representment record for direct comparison against the representment amount to identify partial representments.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: chargeback_reason_code
attributes.description: The original card scheme reason code assigned to the chargeback being rebutted. Retained on the representment for direct reference to understand the basis of the dispute and validate the representment strategy.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the representment record was first created in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. Represents the audit creation time, which may precede the formal submission timestamp.
attributes.references: SOX; PCI DSS; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the representment amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Enables multi-currency dispute processing across the 200+ countries served.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: days_to_deadline
attributes.description: Number of calendar days between the representment creation date and the scheme-mandated response deadline. Positive values indicate days remaining; negative values indicate overdue status. Supports operational prioritization and SLA alerting.

attributes.name: deadline_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the representment was submitted on or before the scheme-mandated response deadline. True if submission_date is on or before response_deadline; False if submitted late. Late submissions are typically rejected by card schemes.

attributes.name: dispute_category
attributes.description: High-level category classifying the nature of the underlying dispute being rebutted. Derived from the chargeback reason code family per card scheme classification. Supports portfolio-level dispute analytics and fraud trend reporting.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; CFPB

attributes.name: evidence_package_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the evidence package submitted with the representment (e.g., document store ID, S3 path, or case management reference). Links to the collection of supporting documents such as transaction receipts, delivery confirmations, and cardholder communications.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: issuing_bank_bin
attributes.description: Bank Identification Number (BIN) / Issuer Identification Number (IIN) of the issuing bank that filed the original chargeback. Used for scheme routing, issuer analysis, and dispute pattern monitoring.
attributes.references: ISO 7812; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current state of the representment in its workflow lifecycle. Tracks progression from initial draft through submission, scheme decision, and potential escalation to pre-arbitration or arbitration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|submitted|accepted|rejected|pre_arbitration|arbitration|closed — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text operational notes added by dispute analysts during the representment lifecycle. Captures escalation rationale, issuer communications, scheme correspondence, and internal case management commentary.

attributes.name: outcome_date
attributes.description: The date on which the card scheme or issuing bank rendered the outcome decision on the representment. Used for cycle time analysis and financial adjustment timing.

attributes.name: outcome_decision
attributes.description: The final or current decision rendered by the card scheme or issuing bank on the representment. Accepted means the chargeback is reversed in the merchant's favor; rejected means the chargeback stands; pre_arbitration and arbitration indicate escalation paths.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: pre_arbitration_deadline
attributes.description: The scheme-mandated deadline by which the acquirer must file for pre-arbitration if the representment is rejected and escalation is desired. Null if pre-arbitration is not applicable or not yet triggered.

attributes.name: pre_arbitration_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this representment is eligible for escalation to the pre-arbitration stage if the outcome decision is rejected. Eligibility is determined by card scheme rules based on reason code, dispute amount, and prior cycle history.

attributes.name: pre_arbitration_filed
attributes.description: Indicates whether a pre-arbitration case has been formally filed following rejection of this representment. True if pre-arbitration has been initiated; False otherwise.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Scheme-specific reason code used by the merchant or acquirer to justify the representment rebuttal. Codes vary by card scheme (e.g., Visa, Mastercard) and correspond to the chargeback reason code being contested. References the dispute reason code reference domain.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: rebuttal_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text narrative written by the merchant or acquirer explaining the basis for the representment rebuttal. Describes why the chargeback is invalid, referencing supporting evidence. Key input for scheme adjudication.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: recovery_amount
attributes.description: The actual monetary amount recovered by the merchant/acquirer following a successful representment outcome. May differ from representment_amount in cases of partial acceptance by the issuer.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: reference
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the representment package, typically assigned by the acquiring bank or payment scheme upon submission. Used for cross-system tracking and scheme correspondence.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: representment_type
attributes.description: Classifies the representment by its position in the dispute cycle. First chargeback representment is the initial rebuttal; second chargeback representment follows a re-presentment rejection; pre-arbitration and arbitration are escalation stages.

attributes.name: response_deadline
attributes.description: The scheme-mandated deadline by which the representment must be submitted to be considered valid. Calculated from the chargeback receipt date per card scheme rules. Critical for SLA compliance monitoring.

attributes.name: scheme_case_number
attributes.description: The case or tracking number assigned by the card scheme (Visa, Mastercard, etc.) to the representment filing. Used for direct correspondence with the scheme and issuer during the dispute resolution process.

attributes.name: scheme_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged by the card scheme for processing the representment filing. Scheme fees vary by network, dispute stage, and outcome. Tracked for merchant billing and P&L reporting.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: submission_channel
attributes.description: The channel through which the representment package was submitted to the card scheme or issuing bank (e.g., scheme portal, API integration, fax, mail, EDI). Supports operational analysis of submission method efficiency.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the representment package was actually submitted. Used in conjunction with response_deadline to calculate deadline compliance status.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time the representment package was formally submitted to the card scheme or issuing bank. This is the principal business event timestamp for the representment transaction. Critical for deadline compliance tracking.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: transaction_amount
attributes.description: The monetary amount of the original payment transaction being disputed. Provides the baseline for assessing partial chargebacks and representment amounts.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: transaction_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the original transaction amount. May differ from representment_currency in cross-border or Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) scenarios.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: transaction_date
attributes.description: The date of the original payment transaction that is the subject of the chargeback and representment. Retained for time-based eligibility checks and scheme rule validation (e.g., chargeback time limits from transaction date).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the representment record. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data freshness monitoring in the Silver layer.
attributes.references: SOX; PCI DSS; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

products.name: arbitration_case
products.description: Formal arbitration proceeding filed with a card scheme (Visa, Mastercard) when a dispute cannot be resolved through standard chargeback, representment, and pre-arbitration cycles. Captures arbitration case number, linked chargeback ID, filing party (issuer or acquirer), scheme arbitration fee amount, filing date, scheme-mandated response deadline, hearing date, arbitration decision, financial liability assignment, compliance case flag, and case closure date. Tracks the highest-escalation tier of the dispute lifecycle.

attributes.name: arbitration_case_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the arbitration case record in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. Primary key for this entity. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.

attributes.name: assigned_analyst_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal dispute analyst or case manager responsible for managing this arbitration case. PARTY_REFERENCE (internal workforce) for operational accountability and workload reporting.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; CRM - Salesforce

attributes.name: card_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.reference_card_scheme. Business justification: Arbitration procedures differ by card scheme; linking enables accurate arbitration fee calculation.

attributes.name: chargeback_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent chargeback record from which this arbitration case was escalated. Links the arbitration proceeding to its originating chargeback dispute lifecycle.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: ecosystem_partner_id
attributes.description: Reference to the acquiring bank (merchant's bank) involved in the arbitration case. PARTY_REFERENCE for TRANSACTION_HEADER role — links to the acquirer master record.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal dispute analyst or case manager responsible for managing this arbitration case. PARTY_REFERENCE (internal workforce) for operational accountability and workload reporting.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; CRM - Salesforce

attributes.name: merchant_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchant whose transaction is the subject of the arbitration. Links to the merchant master record for reporting, analytics, and merchant-level dispute rate monitoring.
attributes.references: Merchant Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: payment_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.payment_product. Business justification: Arbitration decisions reference product terms and fee structures; linking to payment_product is required for regulatory arbitration reporting.

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Arbitration cases are adjudicated per scheme guidelines; scheme_id links the case to the governing scheme for regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: transaction_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original payment transaction that is the subject of the arbitration dispute. Enables traceability from arbitration back to the originating transaction record.

attributes.name: arbitration_decision
attributes.description: Formal outcome of the card scheme arbitration proceeding. Indicates whether the filing party's position was upheld, the respondent prevailed, liability was split, or the case was withdrawn before decision.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: Acquirer Reference Number uniquely identifying the original transaction within the card scheme network. Used to link the arbitration case to the specific transaction across issuer, acquirer, and scheme systems. Standard 23-digit identifier per card scheme rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: case_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the arbitration case. Tracks progression from initial filing through scheme review, decision issuance, and final closure or withdrawal. LIFECYCLE_STATUS for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: Date on which the arbitration case was formally closed in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System, following decision implementation, financial settlement, or withdrawal. Marks end of the arbitration lifecycle.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: compliance_case_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this arbitration case has been designated as a compliance case (as opposed to a standard chargeback arbitration). Compliance cases arise from violations of card scheme rules rather than transaction disputes and follow a distinct scheme process.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: compliance_violation_type
attributes.description: Type of card scheme rule violation cited in a compliance arbitration case (e.g., late presentment, invalid authorization, data integrity violation). Populated only when compliance_case_flag is true. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: late_presentment|invalid_authorization|data_integrity|security_violation|processing_error|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the arbitration case record was first created in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; SOX; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: decision_date
attributes.description: Date on which the card scheme issued its formal arbitration decision. Used to track scheme turnaround time and trigger post-decision financial adjustment processing.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: decision_rationale
attributes.description: Narrative explanation or scheme-provided rationale for the arbitration decision outcome. Documents the basis for liability assignment and supports internal review, representment analysis, and regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; SOX; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: dispute_amount
attributes.description: Gross monetary amount of the original disputed transaction that is the subject of the arbitration. Expressed in the transaction currency. Part of MONETARY_TRIPLET for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583; PCI DSS

attributes.name: dispute_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the dispute type underlying the arbitration case. Groups reason codes into operational categories for reporting and analytics. Aligns with card scheme dispute category frameworks.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: dispute_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the dispute transaction amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for cross-border dispute processing and FX conversion calculations. Part of MONETARY_TRIPLET.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: escalation_cycle_count
attributes.description: Number of dispute lifecycle cycles (chargeback, representment, pre-arbitration) completed before escalation to formal arbitration. Provides context on the dispute history depth and scheme compliance with mandatory pre-arbitration steps.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: evidence_package_submitted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the responding party has submitted a complete evidence package (representment documentation, transaction records, cardholder communications) in response to the arbitration filing.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: evidence_submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the evidence package was submitted to the card scheme for the arbitration proceeding. Used to verify compliance with scheme-mandated evidence submission deadlines.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the arbitration case was formally filed with the card scheme. BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP (date precision) for the arbitration lifecycle. Used to calculate scheme-mandated response deadlines and compliance with filing windows.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: filing_party
attributes.description: Identifies which party in the payment chain initiated the arbitration filing with the card scheme. Either the issuing bank (cardholder's bank) or the acquiring bank (merchant's bank). Determines the direction of liability argument.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: filing_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time (with timezone offset) when the arbitration case was submitted to the card scheme. Provides exact filing time for SLA tracking and scheme deadline calculations. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: gl_adjustment_date
attributes.description: Date on which the financial liability adjustment was posted to the General Ledger following the arbitration decision. Used for period-end financial reconciliation and revenue recognition in Oracle Financials.
attributes.references: ERP - Oracle Financials; SOX; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: gl_adjustment_posted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the financial liability adjustment resulting from the arbitration decision has been posted to the General Ledger in Oracle Financials. Supports financial close reconciliation and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: ERP - Oracle Financials; SOX; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: hearing_date
attributes.description: Scheduled or actual date of the formal arbitration hearing or review session conducted by the card scheme. May be null if the scheme resolves the case on documentary evidence without a formal hearing.

attributes.name: internal_case_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for internal operational notes, analyst observations, and case management commentary related to the arbitration proceeding. Not shared with the card scheme; used for internal dispute team coordination.

attributes.name: issuer_bin
attributes.description: Bank Identification Number (BIN) / Issuer Identification Number (IIN) of the issuing bank involved in the arbitration. Used to identify the card-issuing institution and route scheme communications. 6-8 digit prefix per ISO 7812.
attributes.references: ISO 7812; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS

attributes.name: liability_amount
attributes.description: Net monetary amount of financial liability assigned to the losing party following the arbitration decision. Represents the final financial obligation resulting from the arbitration outcome. Part of MONETARY_TRIPLET — net total component.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: liability_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the financial liability assignment amount. Ensures accurate multi-currency financial reporting and GL posting.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: liable_party
attributes.description: Party assigned financial liability by the card scheme arbitration decision. Determines which entity bears the financial loss from the disputed transaction and scheme fees.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: mid
attributes.description: Merchant Identification Number assigned by the acquirer to uniquely identify the merchant in card scheme communications. Distinct from the internal merchant_id surrogate key; this is the scheme-facing identifier used in dispute and arbitration filings.
attributes.references: Merchant Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: original_transaction_date
attributes.description: Date of the original payment transaction that is the subject of the arbitration dispute. Used for aging analysis, scheme filing window compliance verification, and statute of limitations assessment.
attributes.references: ISO 8583; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: pre_arbitration_cycle_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the mandatory pre-arbitration cycle (second chargeback and pre-arbitration exchange) was completed before escalation to formal arbitration. Required by card scheme rules before arbitration filing is accepted.

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Card scheme-specific reason code classifying the nature of the dispute underlying the arbitration (e.g., Visa reason code 10.4 for fraud, Mastercard reason code 4853 for cardholder dispute). Governs applicable arbitration rules and evidence requirements.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: response_deadline
attributes.description: Card scheme-mandated deadline by which the responding party (issuer or acquirer) must submit their arbitration response package. Failure to respond by this date results in automatic liability assignment per scheme rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: scheme_arbitration_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged by the card scheme for processing the arbitration case. Typically assessed against the losing party per scheme rules. Part of MONETARY_TRIPLET — adjustment/fee component. Amount in scheme fee currency.

attributes.name: scheme_case_number
attributes.description: Externally assigned arbitration case number issued by the card scheme (Visa or Mastercard) upon formal arbitration filing. This is the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER used by all parties and the scheme to reference the proceeding. Format varies by scheme.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; EMVCo

attributes.name: scheme_fee_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the scheme arbitration fee amount. May differ from the dispute transaction currency for cross-border cases.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the arbitration case record. RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Used for incremental data pipeline processing and audit trail maintenance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; SOX; GDPR Article 5

products.name: dispute_case
products.description: Unified dispute case record that serves as the top-level container aggregating all dispute activities — retrieval requests, chargebacks, representments, arbitration proceedings, and financial adjustments — for a single disputed transaction. Captures case number, originating transaction ARN, dispute type (fraud, authorization, processing error, consumer dispute, compliance), case open date, case close date, current lifecycle stage, assigned analyst, and final resolution outcome. SSOT for end-to-end dispute tracking.

attributes.name: dispute_case_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate primary key for the dispute case record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Serves as the top-level container identifier for all dispute activities associated with a single disputed transaction.

attributes.name: account_holder_id
attributes.description: Internal surrogate identifier of the cardholder who initiated or is associated with the dispute. Links to the Cardholder domain for identity, contact, and account details.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; CFPB Regulation E; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: analyst_employee_id
