attributes.description: Internal surrogate identifier of the dispute analyst or case worker currently assigned to manage and resolve this dispute case. Used for workload management, SLA tracking, and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: Internal Dispute Operations Standard; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: authorization_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transaction.authorization. Business justification: Case analysts need original auth details (auth code, response) to determine liability and compliance outcomes.

attributes.name: capture_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transaction.capture. Business justification: Capture information supports accurate calculation of disputed amounts and fee reversals in case settlements.

attributes.name: card_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.reference_card_scheme. Business justification: Chargeback timelines and liability depend on card scheme; linking to reference_card_scheme standardizes rules.

attributes.name: cardholder_profile_id
attributes.description: Internal surrogate identifier of the cardholder who initiated or is associated with the dispute. Links to the Cardholder domain for identity, contact, and account details.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; CFPB Regulation E; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: compliance_aml_screening_result_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Compliance Aml Screening Result Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_aml_screening_result. Business justification: AML screening is performed on entities involved in a dispute; attaching the screening result to the case supports compliance decision‑making.

attributes.name: compliance_kyc_verification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_kyc_verification. Business justification: KYC verification of the cardholder is required for dispute investigation; linking the case to the KYC verification record ensures proper due‑diligence.

attributes.name: cross_border_payment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fx.cross_border_payment. Business justification: Dispute cases originating from cross‑border payments need the payment reference for compliance and routing analysis.

attributes.name: currency_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.currency. Business justification: Currency conversion and cross‑border reporting require a stable ISO currency reference.

attributes.name: digital_wallet_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to wallet.digital_wallet. Business justification: Regulatory and analytics reports need to know which digital wallet originated a dispute case, so a FK from dispute case to digital_wallet is essential.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Internal surrogate identifier of the dispute analyst or case worker currently assigned to manage and resolve this dispute case. Used for workload management, SLA tracking, and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: Internal Dispute Operations Standard; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.gl_account. Business justification: Case settlement accounting: dispute case settlements affect GL accounts; linking enables accurate ledger posting and reconciliation.

attributes.name: mcc_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.mcc. Business justification: Regulatory reporting aggregates disputes by MCC; linking to reference.mcc ensures consistent classification.

attributes.name: merchant_id
attributes.description: Internal surrogate identifier of the merchant involved in the disputed transaction. Links to the Merchant domain for merchant profile, MID, and acquiring relationship context.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; Mastercard Rules; Visa Core Rules

attributes.name: payment_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.payment_product. Business justification: Dispute case workflow applies product‑specific handling rules and compliance checks; a direct FK to payment_product supports rule engine decisions.

attributes.name: payment_txn_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transaction.payment_txn. Business justification: Dispute case reports reference the original payment transaction to provide a complete audit trail and regulatory evidence.

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: Regulatory reporting requires each dispute case to reference the specific regulatory obligation (e.g., PSD2, PCI DSS) it falls under for compliance audits.

attributes.name: request_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gateway.gateway_request. Business justification: Dispute investigation report requires original gateway request details to trace request parameters, timestamps, and merchant context.

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Each dispute case follows the rules of a card scheme; linking to scheme supports the Dispute Case Management report per scheme.

attributes.name: transaction_id
attributes.description: Internal surrogate identifier of the originating payment transaction that is the subject of this dispute case. Links to the Transaction domain SSOT for full transaction context including amount, merchant, and cardholder details.

attributes.name: arbitration_filing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the dispute was escalated to card scheme arbitration after pre-arbitration failed to reach resolution. Null if the case did not reach arbitration. Arbitration decisions are binding and final per card scheme rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules Dispute Resolution; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; Visa Dispute Resolution Management

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: Acquirer Reference Number — the 23-digit unique identifier assigned by the acquiring bank to the originating transaction. Primary linkage key between the dispute case and the underlying payment transaction across card scheme networks. SSOT linkage field per ISO 8583 and card scheme rules.
attributes.references: ISO 8583; Visa Core Rules Section 5; Mastercard Rules Chapter 3

attributes.name: case_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the dispute case, assigned by the Dispute and Chargeback Management System at case creation. Used in all correspondence with cardholders, merchants, and card schemes. Format: DSP-{YYYY}-{8-digit sequence}.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Internal Dispute Operations Standard

attributes.name: case_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the dispute case within the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. Distinct from lifecycle_stage — status reflects the internal workflow state (e.g., awaiting merchant response, under analyst review) while lifecycle_stage reflects the card scheme process stage.
attributes.references: Internal Dispute Operations Standard; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: chargeback_filing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the formal chargeback was filed with the card scheme by the issuing bank. Marks the start of the chargeback lifecycle stage and triggers merchant response deadlines. Null if the case has not yet reached chargeback stage.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: chargeback_reason_code
attributes.description: Card scheme-specific reason code assigned to the chargeback, identifying the precise basis for the dispute (e.g., Visa reason code 10.4 for Other Fraud — Card Absent, Mastercard reason code 4853 for Cardholder Dispute). Null for retrieval requests that have not yet escalated to chargeback. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product — codes vary by card scheme and are subject to periodic updates by Visa, Mastercard, Amex, and Discover]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules Dispute Resolution; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; Amex Dispute Resolution Procedures

attributes.name: close_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the dispute case was formally closed and all activities concluded. Null if the case is still open. Used to calculate total case duration and measure resolution cycle time against SLA targets.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this dispute case record was first created in the data platform. Audit trail field for data lineage and SOX compliance. May differ from open_timestamp if there is a lag between case opening in the source system and ingestion into the lakehouse.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5(2); Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: dispute_amount
attributes.description: The gross monetary amount under dispute, expressed in the transaction currency. Represents the full or partial amount of the original transaction being contested. Used for financial adjustment calculations and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; CFPB Regulation E; PCI DSS

attributes.name: dispute_channel
attributes.description: Channel through which the cardholder or issuing bank initiated the dispute. Values: online (web portal), phone (call center), branch (in-person), mobile_app (mobile banking app), scheme_portal (direct card scheme submission). Used for channel analytics and process optimization.
attributes.references: CFPB Regulation E; Internal Dispute Operations Standard; Visa Dispute Resolution Management

attributes.name: dispute_type
attributes.description: High-level classification of the dispute category as defined by card scheme rules. Values: fraud (unauthorized transaction), authorization (authorization-related issue), processing_error (duplicate, incorrect amount, etc.), consumer_dispute (goods/services not received or not as described), compliance (regulatory or scheme compliance violation).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules Dispute Resolution; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; ISO 8583

attributes.name: evidence_submitted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the merchant has submitted an evidence package (e.g., transaction receipts, delivery confirmation, signed authorization) in response to the chargeback. True = evidence package received. Used to track representment completeness and SLA compliance.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules Dispute Resolution; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; Internal Dispute Operations Standard

attributes.name: interchange_fee_amount
attributes.description: Interchange Reimbursement Fee amount associated with the disputed transaction, which may be reversed or adjusted as part of the chargeback process. Relevant for financial reconciliation between the acquiring bank and issuing bank.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Federal Reserve Regulation II (Durbin Amendment)

attributes.name: is_3ds_authenticated
attributes.description: Indicates whether the original transaction was authenticated using 3-D Secure (3DS) protocol at the time of authorization. True = 3DS authentication was performed. Relevant for liability shift determination — 3DS-authenticated transactions shift chargeback liability to the issuer.
attributes.references: EMVCo 3-D Secure Specification; Visa Secure (Verified by Visa); Mastercard Identity Check; PSD2 SCA Requirements

attributes.name: is_fraud_confirmed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the dispute has been confirmed as a fraudulent transaction by the fraud investigation team or card scheme ruling. True = confirmed fraud; False = not confirmed as fraud. Used for fraud analytics, SAR filing decisions, and AML reporting.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA/SAR Filing Requirements; FATF Recommendation 20; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: issuing_bank_bin
attributes.description: Bank Identification Number (BIN) / Issuer Identification Number (IIN) of the issuing bank that initiated the dispute on behalf of the cardholder. First 6-8 digits of the PAN identifying the card issuer. Used for dispute routing and interchange settlement.
attributes.references: ISO 7812; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this dispute case record in the data platform. Used for incremental ETL processing, change detection, and audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5(2); Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: liability_party
attributes.description: The party determined to bear financial liability for the disputed transaction based on card scheme rules, authentication status, and dispute outcome. Drives financial adjustment routing between issuing bank, acquiring bank, and merchant.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; EMVCo 3DS Liability Shift Rules; PSD2 Article 74

attributes.name: lifecycle_stage
attributes.description: Current stage in the dispute lifecycle workflow as governed by card scheme rules. Progresses from retrieval_request through chargeback, representment, pre_arbitration, arbitration, to closed. Drives SLA deadlines and permissible actions at each stage.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules Dispute Resolution; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; Visa Dispute Resolution Management

attributes.name: mid
attributes.description: Merchant Identification Number assigned by the acquiring bank to uniquely identify the merchant in card scheme networks. Denormalized from the merchant record for direct dispute reporting and card scheme submission without requiring a join.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS Requirement 12

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing analyst notes, investigation findings, key decisions, and case narrative throughout the dispute lifecycle. Supports audit trail requirements and knowledge transfer between analysts. Not intended for structured data — structured fields take precedence.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Dispute Operations Standard; GDPR Article 5(2)

attributes.name: open_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the dispute case was formally opened in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. Serves as the principal business event timestamp and the anchor for all SLA deadline calculations per card scheme rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; CFPB Regulation E 12 CFR Part 1005

attributes.name: original_transaction_amount
attributes.description: The full monetary amount of the original payment transaction that is the subject of this dispute, in the original transaction currency. Provides context for partial dispute scenarios where dispute_amount is less than the full transaction value.
attributes.references: ISO 8583; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: original_transaction_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code of the original payment transaction. May differ from dispute_currency_code in Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) scenarios or cross-border transactions.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; ISO 8583; ISO 20022; Visa Core Rules

attributes.name: original_transaction_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the original payment transaction was processed. Used to calculate dispute filing timeliness against card scheme deadlines (e.g., Visa's 120-day chargeback window from transaction date).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; CFPB Regulation E 12 CFR Part 1005

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Operational priority assigned to the dispute case for analyst workqueue management. Critical cases (e.g., large-value disputes, regulatory escalations, VIP cardholders) receive expedited handling. Drives SLA tier assignment and escalation workflows.
attributes.references: Internal Dispute Operations Standard; Internal SLA Policy

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dispute case is subject to mandatory regulatory reporting obligations (e.g., CFPB complaint reporting, PSD2 incident reporting, OFAC screening result). True = case must be included in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CFPB Regulation E; PSD2 Article 96; OFAC Sanctions Compliance; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: representment_date
attributes.description: Date on which the merchant submitted a representment (rebuttal) package challenging the chargeback. Null if no representment has been filed. Used to track merchant response timeliness and advance the lifecycle stage.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules Dispute Resolution; Mastercard Chargeback Guide

attributes.name: resolution_outcome
attributes.description: Final resolution outcome of the dispute case once closed. Indicates whether the dispute was resolved in favor of the cardholder (won), merchant (lost), mutually settled, withdrawn by the initiating party, written off, or partially recovered. Populated only when case_status = closed.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules Dispute Resolution; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: response_due_date
attributes.description: Deadline by which the merchant or acquiring bank must submit a representment response or evidence package for the current lifecycle stage. Calculated per card scheme rules (e.g., Visa allows 30 days for representment). Breach of this date results in automatic case loss.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules Dispute Resolution; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; Visa Dispute Resolution Management

attributes.name: retrieval_request_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier assigned to the pre-chargeback retrieval request (also known as a copy request) issued by the issuing bank to obtain transaction documentation from the acquirer. Null if the case was filed directly as a chargeback without a prior retrieval request.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; ISO 8583

attributes.name: sar_filed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) was filed with FinCEN in connection with this dispute case due to suspected money laundering, fraud patterns, or other financial crimes identified during the dispute investigation.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA SAR Filing Requirements 31 CFR 1020.320; FATF Recommendation 20; BSA Section 5318(g)

attributes.name: scheme_case_reference
attributes.description: Reference number assigned by the card scheme (Visa, Mastercard, etc.) to track the dispute within their own dispute management system (e.g., Visa Resolve Online - VROL, Mastercard Connect). Used for cross-referencing internal records with scheme-side tracking.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Visa Dispute Resolution Management (VROL)

attributes.name: settlement_adjustment_amount
attributes.description: Net financial adjustment amount applied to the settlement account as a result of the dispute resolution. May differ from dispute_amount due to partial recoveries, fees, or write-offs. Negative value indicates a debit to the merchant; positive indicates a credit to the cardholder.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Chargeback Guide; ERP - Oracle Financials AR/AP; SOX Section 404

products.name: evidence_package
products.description: Collection of evidentiary documents and artifacts assembled to support a representment, pre-arbitration, or arbitration response. Each package contains one or more individual evidence documents tracked at the document level (type, file reference, upload timestamp, validity status). Captures package ID, linked dispute case ID, representment ID, evidence types included (authorization record, delivery confirmation, cardholder communication, AVS/CVV match result, 3DS authentication proof, signed receipt, shipping record), document count, total file size, package assembly date, submission timestamp, submission channel, and package status. Manages the full evidence lifecycle from document collection through scheme submission and supports granular per-document tracking within the package.

attributes.name: evidence_package_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the evidence package record in the dispute and chargeback management system. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: card_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.reference_card_scheme. Business justification: Evidence packages must follow scheme‑specific documentation standards; reference provides authoritative codes.

attributes.name: chargeback_reason_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.chargeback_reason_code. Business justification: Reason codes drive evidence requirements; linking to reference ensures correct code usage.

attributes.name: dispute_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent dispute case to which this evidence package belongs. Links the package to the full dispute lifecycle record.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Username or employee identifier of the dispute analyst or system process that assembled the evidence package. Used for accountability, quality review, and workload reporting.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; SOX

attributes.name: merchant_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchant whose transaction is being disputed. The Merchant Identification Number (MID) links the evidence package to the merchant profile in the Merchant Management System for SLA tracking and reporting.
attributes.references: Merchant Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: representment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the representment filing associated with this evidence package. A representment is the merchant's formal rebuttal to a chargeback, supported by this evidence package.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Evidence packages are assembled according to scheme‑specific requirements; scheme_id enables validation against scheme rules.

attributes.name: acquirer_reference
attributes.description: The acquiring bank's internal reference or case number for this dispute, used for cross-referencing with the acquiring bank's dispute management records and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: The Acquirer Reference Number (ARN) of the original transaction being disputed. A 23-digit unique identifier assigned by the acquiring bank that links the evidence package to the specific settled transaction across card scheme networks.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: assembly_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the evidence package was fully assembled and marked ready for submission. Represents the principal business event time for this entity — the moment the package became a complete evidentiary artifact.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this evidence package record was first created in the dispute management system. Used for audit trail and SLA tracking.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; SOX; PCI DSS

attributes.name: disputed_transaction_amount
attributes.description: The monetary amount of the original transaction being disputed, in the transaction currency. Used to assess financial exposure and validate that the evidence package addresses the correct transaction value.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583; PCI DSS

attributes.name: disputed_transaction_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the disputed transaction amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for cross-border dispute processing and FX-related chargeback reason codes.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: document_count
attributes.description: Total number of individual evidence documents included in this package. Used for completeness validation and scheme submission compliance checks.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: evidence_types_included
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of evidence type codes included in this package (e.g., 'AUTH_RECORD|DELIVERY_CONF|3DS_PROOF'). Provides a consolidated summary of all evidence categories present without requiring a join to the document-level detail table.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: has_3ds_authentication_proof
attributes.description: Indicates whether the evidence package includes 3-D Secure (3DS) authentication proof (e.g., authentication value, ECI indicator, CAVV) demonstrating the transaction was authenticated under PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) requirements.
attributes.references: EMVCo 3DS Specification; PSD2; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: has_authorization_record
attributes.description: Indicates whether the evidence package includes an authorization record (approval code, authorization timestamp, and response code) as evidence that the transaction was properly authorized at the time of the original payment.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583; Payment Gateway and Authorization Engine

attributes.name: has_avs_cvv_match
attributes.business_glossary_term: Has Address Verification System / Card Verification Value (AVS/CVV) Match Result
attributes.description: Indicates whether the evidence package includes the Address Verification System (AVS) and/or Card Verification Value (CVV) match result from the original authorization, demonstrating the cardholder's identity was verified at point of sale.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS; Payment Gateway and Authorization Engine

attributes.name: has_cardholder_communication
attributes.description: Indicates whether the evidence package includes documented communication with the cardholder (e.g., email correspondence, chat logs, signed agreements) relevant to the disputed transaction.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; GDPR Article 5; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: has_delivery_confirmation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the evidence package includes a delivery confirmation document (e.g., signed proof of delivery, carrier tracking confirmation) to rebut non-receipt chargebacks.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: has_shipping_record
attributes.description: Indicates whether the evidence package includes a shipping record (e.g., carrier waybill, tracking number, shipment manifest) as evidence of goods dispatch for merchandise-related disputes.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: has_signed_receipt
attributes.description: Indicates whether the evidence package includes a signed transaction receipt (physical or electronic) bearing the cardholder's signature or PIN-verified acknowledgment at the point of sale.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; EMVCo; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: is_auto_assembled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the evidence package was assembled automatically by the dispute management system's Straight-Through Processing (STP) engine, or manually by a dispute analyst. Supports STP rate reporting and automation analytics.

attributes.name: issuer_reference
attributes.description: The issuing bank's case or reference number for the chargeback, as communicated in the chargeback notification. Used to correlate the evidence package with the issuer's dispute record.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this evidence package record was most recently modified. Tracks the latest change to any field in the package record for audit and change management purposes.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; SOX; PCI DSS

attributes.name: outcome_date
attributes.description: The date on which the final resolution outcome was received from the card scheme, issuing bank, or arbitration body. Used for financial adjustment processing and dispute analytics.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: outcome_reason
attributes.description: Textual explanation or scheme-provided reason code description for the dispute outcome decision. Captures why the evidence package was accepted or rejected to support root cause analysis and process improvement.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: package_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by the dispute analyst regarding the evidence package, including special circumstances, escalation context, or instructions for the reviewing party. Not transmitted to the card scheme.

attributes.name: package_outcome
attributes.description: Final resolution outcome of the evidence package submission: won (dispute resolved in merchant's favor), lost (chargeback upheld), partial_win (partial amount recovered), withdrawn (package retracted), or pending (awaiting decision).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: package_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to the evidence package, used in scheme submissions and merchant communications. Follows the EVP- prefix convention.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: package_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the evidence package: draft (being assembled), assembled (complete but not yet submitted), submitted (sent to card scheme or issuer), accepted (acknowledged by receiving party), rejected (refused by receiving party), or withdrawn (retracted before decision).
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: package_type
attributes.description: Classification of the evidence package by the dispute stage it supports: representment (first chargeback rebuttal), pre_arbitration (pre-arb response), arbitration (scheme arbitration filing), retrieval_response (response to retrieval request), or good_faith (voluntary compliance submission). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: representment|pre_arbitration|arbitration|retrieval_response|good_faith — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: recovered_amount
attributes.description: The monetary amount recovered in the merchant's favor as a result of the evidence package submission. May be equal to the full disputed amount (full win), a partial amount (partial win), or zero (loss). Denominated in the disputed transaction currency.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: rejection_reason_code
attributes.description: Card scheme or issuer-provided code indicating why the evidence package was rejected (e.g., late submission, insufficient evidence, incorrect format). Populated only when package_status is 'rejected'. Used for defect analysis and process improvement.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: response_deadline_date
attributes.description: The card scheme-mandated deadline by which the evidence package must be submitted to avoid forfeiture of the dispute. Derived from chargeback receipt date plus scheme-specific response windows (e.g., Visa 30 days, Mastercard 45 days).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: scheme_case_number
attributes.description: The card scheme-assigned case or arbitration number for this dispute (e.g., Visa Resolve Online case ID, Mastercard Connect case number). Populated when the dispute has been escalated to scheme-level arbitration.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: scheme_submission_confirmation
attributes.description: Confirmation or acknowledgment number returned by the card scheme portal (e.g., Visa Resolve Online, Mastercard Connect) upon successful receipt of the evidence package submission. Used for reconciliation and proof of timely submission.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: sla_deadline_met
attributes.description: Indicates whether the evidence package was submitted before the card scheme response deadline. False indicates a missed SLA, which results in automatic forfeiture of the dispute. Critical for operational performance monitoring.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: submission_channel
attributes.description: The channel or platform through which the evidence package was submitted to the card scheme or issuer: visa_resolve_online (Visa's dispute portal), mastercard_connect (Mastercard's portal), api (programmatic submission), manual_upload, fax, or email. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: visa_resolve_online|mastercard_connect|api|manual_upload|fax|email — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the evidence package was formally submitted to the card scheme, issuing bank, or arbitration body. Null if the package has not yet been submitted.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: submitted_by_user
attributes.description: Username or employee identifier of the individual or automated process that submitted the evidence package to the card scheme or issuer. Supports audit trail requirements under SOX and PCI DSS.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; SOX; PCI DSS

attributes.name: total_file_size_bytes
attributes.description: Aggregate file size in bytes of all documents included in the evidence package. Used to validate compliance with card scheme maximum submission size limits (e.g., Visa 5MB per package).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

products.name: financial_adjustment
products.description: Financial adjustment record generated as a result of a dispute event — chargeback debit, representment credit, arbitration fee, scheme compliance assessment, or final settlement adjustment. Captures adjustment ID, dispute case ID, adjustment type, adjustment amount, currency, debit/credit indicator, settlement batch reference, GL account code, posting date, reversal flag, and scheme-assigned financial liability party. SSOT for all monetary movements originating from the dispute lifecycle.

attributes.name: financial_adjustment_id
attributes.description: Primary key for financial_adjustment

attributes.name: card_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.reference_card_scheme. Business justification: Adjustments are settled per scheme rules; reference needed for accurate fee and liability handling.

attributes.name: dispute_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent dispute case that triggered this financial adjustment. Links the monetary movement back to the originating dispute lifecycle record.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: ecosystem_partner_id
attributes.description: Reference to the acquiring bank (merchant's bank) responsible for processing the original transaction and managing the financial adjustment in the dispute lifecycle.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Transaction Processing Platform

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.gl_account. Business justification: Adjustment posting: financial adjustments are recorded against a specific GL account to reflect balance‑sheet impact and audit trails.

attributes.name: mcc_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.mcc. Business justification: MCC determines interchange and fee adjustments; linking to reference.mcc standardizes calculations.

attributes.name: merchant_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchant involved in the disputed transaction that generated this financial adjustment. Used for merchant-level dispute reporting, MDR reconciliation, and chargeback ratio monitoring.
attributes.references: Merchant Management System; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: original_transaction_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original payment transaction record that is the subject of the dispute. Enables traceability from the financial adjustment back to the source authorization and capture event.
attributes.references: ISO 8583; Payment Gateway and Authorization Engine; Transaction Processing Platform

attributes.name: rate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fx.fx_rate. Business justification: Financial adjustments often involve currency conversion; audit requires the FX rate used for the adjustment.

attributes.name: reversal_reference_financial_adjustment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original financial adjustment record that this entry reverses. Populated only when reversal_flag is True, enabling full audit trail of reversal chains.
attributes.references: ERP - Oracle Financials; SOX; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Financial adjustments (fees, refunds) are charged per scheme fee schedule; scheme_id ties adjustments to the correct scheme for accounting.

attributes.name: adjustment_amount
attributes.description: Gross monetary value of the financial adjustment in the transaction currency. Represents the principal amount being debited or credited as a result of the dispute event.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: adjustment_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the adjustment amount. Identifies the currency in which the financial adjustment is denominated.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: adjustment_event_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the financial adjustment event was triggered in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. Represents the real-world business event time, distinct from the GL posting date.
attributes.references: ISO 8583; Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Visa Core Rules

attributes.name: adjustment_notes
attributes.description: Free-text operational notes or comments recorded by dispute analysts regarding the financial adjustment, such as manual override justifications, scheme correspondence references, or exception handling details.

attributes.name: adjustment_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this financial adjustment, used in reconciliation, GL posting, and scheme communications. Assigned by the Dispute and Chargeback Management System or card scheme.
attributes.references: ISO 8583; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: adjustment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the financial adjustment record within the dispute processing workflow. Drives GL posting eligibility and settlement batch inclusion.
attributes.references: ERP - Oracle Financials; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: adjustment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the financial adjustment event within the dispute lifecycle. Determines the direction of fund flow and the applicable card scheme rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: chargeback_debit|representment_credit|arbitration_fee|compliance_assessment|final_settlement|pre_arbitration_debit|pre_compliance_fee|good_faith_collection — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: Acquirer Reference Number (ARN) linking this financial adjustment to the original payment transaction. The ARN is the primary cross-system linkage key used by card schemes, acquirers, and issuers to trace dispute-related monetary movements back to the originating transaction.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: auto_posted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this financial adjustment was automatically posted to the GL via Straight-Through Processing (STP) (True) or required manual intervention before posting (False). Supports operational efficiency reporting and STP rate analytics.
attributes.references: ERP - Oracle Financials; Transaction Processing Platform

attributes.name: bin
attributes.description: Bank Identification Number (BIN) / Issuer Identification Number (IIN) of the payment card involved in the disputed transaction. Used for issuer-level dispute analytics and scheme reporting segmentation.
attributes.references: ISO 7812; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS

attributes.name: chargeback_reason_code
attributes.description: Card scheme-assigned reason code classifying the basis for the chargeback or dispute (e.g., Visa reason code 10.4 for fraud, Mastercard reason code 4853 for cardholder dispute). Determines applicable dispute rights, response deadlines, and financial liability rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this financial adjustment record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SLA compliance tracking.
attributes.references: SOX; GDPR Article 5; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: debit_credit_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this financial adjustment represents a debit (funds withdrawn from the merchant or acquirer) or a credit (funds returned). Critical for GL double-entry accounting and settlement reconciliation.
attributes.references: ERP - Oracle Financials; ISO 8583; Visa Core Rules

attributes.name: dispute_resolution_outcome
attributes.description: Final outcome of the dispute case associated with this financial adjustment. Determines whether the adjustment represents a permanent financial liability or will be reversed upon successful representment or arbitration.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: dispute_stage
attributes.description: Stage in the dispute lifecycle at which this financial adjustment was generated. Determines the applicable card scheme rules, financial liability, and response rights for each party.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: financial_period
attributes.description: Accounting period (YYYY-MM) to which this financial adjustment is attributed for revenue recognition, period-end close, and regulatory financial reporting. Aligned with Oracle Financials GL calendar.

attributes.name: fx_conversion_rate
attributes.description: Exchange rate applied when converting the adjustment amount from the transaction currency to the settlement currency. Applicable for cross-border disputes involving Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) or multi-currency settlement.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ECB

attributes.name: gl_cost_center_code
attributes.description: Oracle Financials cost center dimension code associated with this adjustment for internal financial reporting and P&L attribution within the dispute operations function.

attributes.name: interchange_amount
attributes.description: Interchange Reimbursement Fee (IRF) component of the financial adjustment, representing the fee paid between the acquiring bank and issuing bank as part of the dispute resolution. Relevant for chargeback debits and representment credits.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Federal Reserve System Regulation II (Durbin Amendment)

attributes.name: issuer_code
attributes.description: Reference to the issuing bank (cardholder's bank) that initiated the chargeback or dispute. Used for issuer-level financial reporting and scheme compliance tracking.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Transaction Processing Platform

attributes.name: liability_party
attributes.description: Card scheme-assigned party bearing financial liability for this adjustment. Determined by the dispute reason code, evidence outcome, and applicable card scheme rules (Visa Core Rules or Mastercard Rules).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; EMVCo

attributes.name: posting_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the financial adjustment was posted to the General Ledger (GL) and included in the settlement batch. Drives financial period recognition and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ERP - Oracle Financials; SOX; Visa Core Rules

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this financial adjustment must be included in regulatory reports (True), such as FinCEN BSA filings, CFPB complaint reporting, or scheme compliance submissions. Drives automated regulatory data aggregation.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA; CFPB; SOX; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: response_deadline_date
attributes.description: Card scheme-mandated deadline by which the liable party must respond to or contest this financial adjustment. Failure to meet this deadline results in automatic financial liability assignment per Visa or Mastercard rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: reversal_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this financial adjustment has been reversed (True) or remains active (False). A reversal occurs when a chargeback is rescinded, a representment is accepted, or an error correction is applied.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: scheme_case_number
attributes.description: Unique case reference number assigned by the card scheme (Visa or Mastercard) for arbitration or compliance proceedings associated with this financial adjustment. Used for scheme-level dispute tracking and correspondence.

attributes.name: scheme_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee assessed by the card scheme (Visa or Mastercard) for processing the dispute event, such as arbitration filing fees or compliance assessment charges. Included in the net settlement calculation.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI Security Standards Council

attributes.name: settlement_amount
attributes.description: Net amount posted to the settlement batch after applying any scheme fees, interchange adjustments, or currency conversion. May differ from adjustment_amount when FX conversion or fee netting applies.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Transaction Processing Platform

attributes.name: settlement_batch_reference
attributes.description: Identifier of the settlement batch in which this financial adjustment was included for clearing and fund transfer. Links to the Transaction Processing Platform batch processing records.
attributes.references: Transaction Processing Platform; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; NACHA

attributes.name: settlement_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the settlement amount. May differ from adjustment_currency_code when Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) or cross-border settlement applies.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record that originated this financial adjustment record (e.g., Dispute and Chargeback Management System, ERP Oracle Financials, card scheme network feed, or manual entry). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Data Warehouse and Analytics Platform; SOX

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this financial adjustment record. Supports change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX; GDPR Article 5; Data Warehouse and Analytics Platform

products.name: dispute_lifecycle_event
products.description: Immutable event log capturing every state transition and significant activity in a dispute case lifecycle. Captures event ID, dispute case ID, event type (case opened, retrieval sent, chargeback filed, representment submitted, pre-arbitration filed, arbitration decided, case closed, deadline breached), event timestamp, actor type (issuer, acquirer, scheme, merchant, analyst), actor ID, previous state, new state, and event notes. Provides full audit trail for regulatory compliance and dispute analytics.

attributes.name: dispute_lifecycle_event_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each immutable event record in the dispute lifecycle event log. Primary key for this append-only audit table. Role: EVENT_LOG.

attributes.name: card_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.reference_card_scheme. Business justification: Lifecycle events (e.g., deadline breaches) are scheme‑dependent; reference provides rule context.

attributes.name: dispute_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent dispute case that this lifecycle event belongs to. Links all events in the audit trail back to a single dispute case record. EVENT_SOURCE_REFERENCE per EVENT_LOG role.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific party (issuer BIN, acquirer MID, scheme network code, merchant ID, or analyst user ID) that performed this lifecycle event. Provides granular accountability for each state transition. EVENT_SOURCE_REFERENCE complement per EVENT_LOG role.
attributes.references: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10.2; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: evidence_package_id
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the evidence package (documents, transaction records, cardholder correspondence) submitted as part of a representment or arbitration response at this event stage. Links to the document management system within the Dispute and Chargeback Management System.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; PCI DSS v4.0

attributes.name: mcc_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.mcc. Business justification: Event analytics often filter by MCC; linking enables consistent reporting.

attributes.name: original_transaction_id
attributes.description: The internal transaction identifier of the original payment transaction that is the subject of this dispute. Enables cross-referencing with the Transaction Processing Platform for clearing and settlement reconciliation.
attributes.references: ISO 8583; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Transaction Processing Platform

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Lifecycle events track status changes of disputes; scheme_id is needed for the Dispute Lifecycle Dashboard segmented by scheme.

attributes.name: acquirer_mid
attributes.description: The Merchant Identification Number assigned by the acquiring bank to the merchant involved in this dispute event. Used for merchant-level dispute tracking, chargeback ratio monitoring, and acquirer reporting.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583; Merchant Management System

attributes.name: actor_type
attributes.description: Category of the party that triggered or performed this lifecycle event. Identifies whether the action was taken by the issuing bank, acquiring bank, card scheme, merchant, or an internal analyst. Critical for accountability and regulatory audit trails.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: arbitration_outcome
attributes.description: The final decision rendered by the card scheme in arbitration proceedings. Populated only when event_type is arbitration_decided. Determines final financial liability allocation between issuer and acquirer.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: The Acquirer Reference Number uniquely identifying the original financial transaction linked to this dispute event. Industry-standard 23-digit identifier used by card schemes to trace transactions across the payment network. Enables cross-system reconciliation.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: channel
attributes.description: The payment channel through which the original disputed transaction was conducted. Influences applicable chargeback reason codes, liability rules, and fraud classification under card scheme rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: card_present|card_not_present|atm|contactless|ecommerce|mobile|recurring — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; EMVCo; PSD2 Article 97

attributes.name: chargeback_cycle
attributes.description: Identifies the current cycle stage of the chargeback process at the time of this event. Distinguishes first chargeback from second chargeback (re-presentment response), pre-arbitration, and formal arbitration stages per card scheme rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules Chargeback Guide; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules

attributes.name: chargeback_reason_code
attributes.description: Card scheme-specific reason code classifying the basis for a chargeback filing (e.g., Visa reason code 10.4 for fraud, 13.1 for merchandise not received; Mastercard reason code 4853 for cardholder dispute). Populated when event_type is chargeback_filed or representment_submitted.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules Chargeback Guide; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this lifecycle event record was first written to the data platform. Distinct from event_timestamp (business event time). Used for data lineage, ETL audit trails, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10; SOX; GDPR Article 5(2)

attributes.name: dispute_amount
attributes.description: The monetary value under dispute at the time of this lifecycle event, expressed in the dispute currency. May differ from the original transaction amount due to partial chargebacks or adjustments applied during the dispute process.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; CFPB Regulation E; SOX

attributes.name: dispute_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the dispute amount at the time of this event (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for cross-border dispute processing and FX reconciliation.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 20022

attributes.name: event_notes
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the context, rationale, or outcome of this lifecycle event. Captures analyst commentary, scheme decision rationale, or system-generated explanations. EVENT_PAYLOAD_OR_VALUE per EVENT_LOG role.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: event_sequence_number
attributes.description: Monotonically increasing sequence number of this event within the parent dispute case, starting at 1 for the first event. Enables ordered reconstruction of the complete dispute lifecycle timeline and detection of out-of-order event ingestion.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which this lifecycle event occurred. Authoritative event time used for SLA deadline tracking, regulatory audit trails, and dispute analytics. Conforms to yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format. EVENT_TIMESTAMP per EVENT_LOG role.
attributes.references: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10.3; ISO 8583; Visa Core Rules Section 5

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Discriminator classifying the kind of lifecycle event that occurred in the dispute workflow. Drives downstream routing, SLA monitoring, and regulatory reporting. EVENT_TYPE_OR_CHANNEL per EVENT_LOG role. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: case_opened|retrieval_sent|chargeback_filed|representment_submitted|pre_arbitration_filed|arbitration_decided|case_closed|deadline_breached — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: financial_adjustment_amount
attributes.description: The monetary value of the financial adjustment (debit, credit, fee, or reversal) associated with this lifecycle event. Used for settlement reconciliation, GL posting, and dispute financial reporting. Expressed in dispute_currency_code.
attributes.references: SOX; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials; ISO 20022

attributes.name: financial_adjustment_type
attributes.description: Classifies the type of financial adjustment triggered by this lifecycle event (e.g., debit to acquirer for chargeback, credit to issuer, reversal for representment win, scheme fee). Drives GL posting and settlement reconciliation in ERP - Oracle Financials.
attributes.references: SOX; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 20022; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: is_deadline_breached
attributes.description: Indicates whether the response deadline for this lifecycle event stage was breached (True) or met on time (False). Drives automatic escalation workflows, scheme penalty assessments, and SLA reporting.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: is_fraud_related
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dispute event is classified as fraud-related (True) based on the chargeback reason code or fraud detection platform signals. Drives SAR/STR filing obligations, fraud analytics, and scheme fraud reporting thresholds.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA; FATF Recommendations; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Fraud Detection and Prevention Platform

attributes.name: issuer_bin
attributes.description: The Bank Identification Number (BIN) / Issuer Identification Number (IIN) of the issuing bank involved in this dispute event. Used for scheme routing, interchange settlement, and issuer-level dispute analytics.
attributes.references: ISO 7812; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: new_state
attributes.description: The dispute case state immediately after this event was applied. Represents the current state of the dispute case as of this event. Used for SLA tracking, workflow routing, and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new|retrieval_pending|chargeback_pending|representment_pending|pre_arbitration_pending|arbitration_pending|resolved|closed — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: original_transaction_date
attributes.description: The date on which the original payment transaction subject to this dispute was processed. Used to calculate dispute filing timeliness, scheme deadline windows, and statute of limitations compliance.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; CFPB Regulation E; ISO 8583

attributes.name: pan_last_four
attributes.business_glossary_term: Primary Account Number (PAN) Last Four Digits
attributes.description: The last four digits of the cardholder's Primary Account Number (PAN) associated with the disputed transaction. Retained for dispute identification and cardholder communication while complying with PCI DSS data minimization requirements.
attributes.references: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 3; ISO 7812; Visa Core Rules

attributes.name: previous_state
attributes.description: The dispute case state immediately before this event was applied. Together with new_state, provides a complete state-transition record for audit and analytics. Enables reconstruction of the full dispute lifecycle history. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new|retrieval_pending|chargeback_pending|representment_pending|pre_arbitration_pending|arbitration_pending|resolved|closed — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: processing_region
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the region where this dispute event was processed. Determines applicable regulatory framework (e.g., PSD2 in EU, Regulation E in US), jurisdiction for compliance reporting, and cross-border dispute rules.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; PSD2; CFPB Regulation E; GDPR; Visa Core Rules

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this lifecycle event triggers a mandatory regulatory reporting obligation (True), such as SAR/STR filing with FinCEN, CFPB complaint reporting, or scheme fraud reporting. Drives compliance workflow routing in the Risk and Compliance Management System.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA; CFPB Regulation E; FATF Recommendations; PSD2; Risk and Compliance Management System

attributes.name: resolution_outcome
attributes.description: The final resolution outcome for the dispute case as recorded at this event. Populated when event_type is case_closed. Indicates whether the dispute was won, lost, partially resolved, withdrawn by the claimant, or expired due to deadline breach.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: response_deadline
attributes.description: The date and time by which the responding party (acquirer, merchant, or issuer) must submit their response or evidence package for this event stage. Derived from card scheme rules and the event timestamp. Critical for SLA breach detection.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: response_submitted_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time at which the required response or evidence package was submitted for this event stage. Compared against response_deadline to determine SLA compliance and deadline breach status.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10

attributes.name: retrieval_request_number
attributes.description: The unique reference number assigned to a retrieval request (pre-chargeback inquiry) issued by the issuing bank to obtain transaction documentation. Populated when event_type is retrieval_sent. Precedes formal chargeback filing in the dispute lifecycle.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: scheme_case_reference
attributes.description: The external case or tracking reference number assigned by the card scheme (Visa, Mastercard, etc.) for this dispute. Used for cross-referencing with scheme portals (e.g., Visa Resolve Online - VROL, Mastercard Connect) and scheme correspondence.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: scheme_fee_amount
attributes.description: The fee levied by the card scheme (Visa, Mastercard, etc.) for processing this dispute event stage (e.g., arbitration filing fee, chargeback processing fee). Expressed in dispute_currency_code. Used for cost allocation and P&L reporting.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials; SOX

attributes.name: sla_target_hours
attributes.description: The number of hours within which the required action for this event type must be completed per card scheme rules and internal SLA commitments. Used to compute response_deadline and monitor SLA compliance.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Dispute Resolution Rules; Internal SLA Policy

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record that originated this lifecycle event record (e.g., Dispute and Chargeback Management System, Payment Gateway and Authorization Engine). Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and Silver layer provenance tracking.
attributes.references: SOX; PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10; Data Warehouse and Analytics Platform

attributes.name: three_ds_authentication_result
attributes.description: The outcome of 3-D Secure (3DS) authentication for the original disputed transaction. Determines liability shift applicability under card scheme rules — authenticated transactions shift liability to the issuer, affecting dispute outcome and representment strategy.
attributes.references: EMVCo 3DS Specification; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PSD2 SCA Requirements

products.name: pre_arbitration
products.description: Pre-arbitration filing record representing the escalation step between representment rejection and formal arbitration. Captures pre-arbitration ID, linked chargeback ID, linked representment ID, filing party (issuer or acquirer), filing date, scheme pre-arbitration case number, scheme-mandated response deadline, actual response date, deadline compliance status, response received flag, outcome (accepted, rejected, escalated to arbitration), and financial liability amount. Tracks the intermediate escalation tier before formal scheme arbitration.

attributes.name: pre_arbitration_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the pre-arbitration case record. Primary key for the pre-arbitration entity.
attributes.references: ISO 8583 Financial Transaction Card Messaging Standard

attributes.name: assigned_analyst_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the dispute analyst or case manager responsible for managing this pre-arbitration case.

attributes.name: card_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.reference_card_scheme. Business justification: Pre‑arbitration timelines vary by scheme; reference needed for SLA monitoring.

attributes.name: chargeback_id
attributes.description: Reference to the originating chargeback case that was escalated to pre-arbitration after representment rejection.

attributes.name: ecosystem_partner_id
attributes.description: Bank Identification Number (BIN) or Issuer Identification Number (IIN) of the cardholder's issuing bank, typically the first 6-11 digits of the card number.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the dispute analyst or case manager responsible for managing this pre-arbitration case.

attributes.name: merchant_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchant whose transaction is subject to this pre-arbitration case.

attributes.name: representment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the representment case that was rejected by the issuer, triggering this pre-arbitration escalation.

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Pre‑arbitration processes follow scheme‑defined timelines; scheme_id links each pre‑arbitration record to its governing scheme.

attributes.name: transaction_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original payment transaction that is the subject of this pre-arbitration dispute.

attributes.name: acquirer_bank_code
attributes.description: Bank Identification Number (BIN) of the merchant's acquiring bank that processed the original transaction.

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: Unique 23-digit reference number assigned by the acquiring bank to track the transaction through the dispute lifecycle, including pre-arbitration.

attributes.name: case_notes
attributes.description: Internal notes and commentary regarding the pre-arbitration case, including strategy considerations, evidence assessment, and communication history.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pre-arbitration record was first created in the dispute management system.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls, Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the liability amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: deadline_compliance_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the responding party met the scheme-mandated response deadline: compliant (on time), late (submitted after deadline but accepted), or missed (no response submitted).

attributes.name: escalation_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the case was escalated to pre-arbitration after representment rejection, including the basis for challenging the issuer's decision.

attributes.name: evidence_submission_count
attributes.description: Number of evidence documents or packages submitted by the filing party to support their pre-arbitration claim.

attributes.name: fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged by the card scheme for filing a pre-arbitration case. This fee is typically assessed to the losing party upon case resolution.

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: Date when the pre-arbitration case was officially filed with the card scheme by the filing party.

attributes.name: filing_party
attributes.description: Identifies which party initiated the pre-arbitration: issuer (cardholder's bank) or acquirer (merchant's bank).

attributes.name: filing_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the pre-arbitration case was submitted to the card scheme system, including time zone information.

attributes.name: liability_amount
attributes.description: Financial amount in dispute for this pre-arbitration case, representing the transaction amount plus any applicable fees that will be assigned to the losing party.

attributes.name: liability_party
attributes.description: Party assigned financial liability for the disputed transaction as a result of the pre-arbitration outcome: issuer (cardholder's bank), acquirer (merchant's bank), merchant, or pending (not yet determined).

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pre-arbitration record was last updated, tracking any changes to status, outcome, or case details.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls, Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: outcome
attributes.description: Final outcome of the pre-arbitration case: accepted (filing party wins, liability assigned), rejected (responding party wins, original decision stands), escalated_to_arbitration (unresolved, proceeding to formal arbitration), withdrawn (filing party withdrew claim), or pending (outcome not yet determined).
attributes.references: Visa Dispute Resolution Rules, Mastercard Chargeback Guide

attributes.name: pre_arbitration_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the pre-arbitration case: filed (submitted to scheme), pending_response (awaiting counterparty response), under_review (scheme reviewing submissions), accepted (pre-arb claim accepted), rejected (pre-arb claim denied), escalated_to_arbitration (proceeding to formal arbitration), withdrawn (filing party withdrew), or expired (deadline passed without resolution). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: filed|pending_response|under_review|accepted|rejected|escalated_to_arbitration|withdrawn|expired — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Card scheme-specific reason code that categorizes the dispute type (e.g., Visa 10.4 Fraud, Mastercard 4853 Cardholder Dispute). Inherited from the originating chargeback.
attributes.references: Visa Reason Code Guide, Mastercard Chargeback Reason Code List

attributes.name: reason_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the chargeback reason code explaining the nature of the dispute (e.g., 'Fraudulent Transaction - Card Not Present').

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: Date when the pre-arbitration case reached final resolution (accepted, rejected, or escalated to arbitration). Null if case is still pending.

attributes.name: response_date
attributes.description: Actual date when the responding party submitted their response to the pre-arbitration case. Null if no response has been received.

attributes.name: response_deadline_date
attributes.description: Card scheme-mandated deadline by which the responding party must submit their response to the pre-arbitration filing. Typically 10-45 days depending on scheme and reason code.
attributes.references: Visa Dispute Resolution Rules, Mastercard Chargeback Guide

attributes.name: response_received_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether a response has been received from the responding party. True if response submitted, False if pending or no response.

attributes.name: response_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the response was received by the card scheme system, used for deadline compliance verification.

attributes.name: scheme_case_number
attributes.description: Unique case identifier assigned by the card scheme (Visa, Mastercard, etc.) for tracking the pre-arbitration proceeding within their dispute resolution system.
attributes.references: Visa Dispute Resolution Rules, Mastercard Chargeback Guide

attributes.name: scheme_decision_date
attributes.description: Date when the card scheme issued their official decision on the pre-arbitration case, determining liability assignment.
attributes.references: Visa Dispute Resolution Rules, Mastercard Chargeback Guide

attributes.name: withdrawal_date
attributes.description: Date when the filing party voluntarily withdrew the pre-arbitration case. Null if case was not withdrawn.

attributes.name: withdrawal_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why the filing party withdrew the pre-arbitration case, such as settlement reached, insufficient evidence, or strategic decision.

products.name: rule_config
products.description: Business rule configuration governing automated dispute handling decisions — auto-accept thresholds, auto-representment eligibility criteria, reason-code-specific response strategies, merchant-level dispute handling overrides, and scheme-specific processing rules. Captures rule ID, rule name, rule type, applicable reason code scope, merchant segment scope, threshold amount, currency, auto-action type, effective date, expiry date, and approval status. Enables configurable dispute automation without code changes.

attributes.name: rule_config_id
attributes.description: Primary key for rule_config

attributes.name: card_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.reference_card_scheme. Business justification: Rule engine applies scheme‑specific thresholds; linking ensures correct rule application.

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Dispute rule configurations are defined per card scheme; scheme_id is required for the Rule Engine to select appropriate rules.

attributes.name: action_parameters
attributes.description: Configuration parameters or metadata required to execute the auto action, stored as JSON or key-value pairs.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Approval workflow status indicating whether the rule configuration has been reviewed and authorized for production use.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Identifier or name of the user or role who approved this rule configuration for production deployment.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this rule configuration was approved, recorded in ISO 8601 format.

attributes.name: auto_action_type
attributes.description: Automated action to be taken when the rule conditions are met during dispute processing.

attributes.name: compliance_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing compliance considerations, regulatory alignment, or audit notes related to this rule configuration.

attributes.name: condition_expression
attributes.description: Structured or semi-structured expression defining the logical conditions under which this rule is triggered. May be JSON, XML, or domain-specific language.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this dispute rule configuration record was first created in the system, recorded in ISO 8601 format.

attributes.name: dispute_age_threshold_days
attributes.description: Maximum age of the dispute in days for this rule to apply, enabling time-sensitive rule logic.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this dispute rule configuration becomes active and applicable to dispute processing.

attributes.name: evidence_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether supporting evidence must be present for the rule action to be executed.

attributes.name: evidence_type_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated or pipe-separated list of evidence types required for this rule to trigger, such as delivery_confirmation, signature, invoice.

attributes.name: execution_count
attributes.description: Cumulative count of how many times this rule has been executed since activation, used for monitoring and analytics.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this dispute rule configuration ceases to be active. Null indicates no expiration.

attributes.name: failure_count
attributes.description: Cumulative count of failed rule executions where the rule action could not be completed due to errors or exceptions.

attributes.name: is_active
